newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Monde-Buba contests its Tietmeyer translation.
newsitem.headline: Le Monde-Buba contests its Tietmeyer translation.

text.p: French afternoon daily Le Monde said on Friday that the Bundesbank had contested its translation of comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer when it quoted him as saying there was room for interpretation of Maastricht treaty criteria.
In an interview published on Wednesday it reported that Tietmeyer had said that there was room for interpretation in Maastricht treaty criteria but this must be strict.
The Bundesbank gave the following official translation in English of the contested comment in the interview, which was conducted in German:

"The treaty contains figures on the one hand and besides that also additional verbal qualifications. In the opinion of the Bundesbank and the federal government -- and here the Bundesbank and the federal government agree completely -- those qualifications as well as the numbers must be strictly interpreted and fulfilled."
Le Monde said it stood by its translation, which it said was in line with an interpretation of the treaty by French experts.
